To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

3He, and more in general nuclei with an odd number of neutrons, are very promising for the determination of the neutron orbital angular momentum and that the coherent DVCS off 3He is an ideal tool for such a determination.

(a) the neutron information is largely dominant in the 3He DVCS, (b) the IA analysis is able to provide a good description of the 3He GPDs, (c) the neutron orbital angular momentum is largely dominated by the orbital angular momentum carried by the valence quarks.

1) The neutron GPDs are accessible in coherent deeply virtual compton scattering (DVCSV), in the impulse approximation, with a large signal, and 2) The extraction of the neutron GPD from coherent DVCS on 3He requires an analysis of the experimental data in terms of a model that includes the nuclear effects, such as the Fermi motion and the off-shellness of the nucleons, that are included in the IA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nucleon and nuclear structure through the analysis of the generalized parton distributions of the nucleons and the nuclei.
the study of the structure of the nucleon in terms of its partonic constituents.
the study of the nucleon structure, with a particular focus on the neutron, through the study of the generalized parton distributions of 3He.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coherent DVCS on 3He is a very promising tool to investigate the neutron structure.

the 3He GPDs are very interesting for the extraction of neutron GPDs, which are very interesting for accessing neutron orbital angular momentum, which is very interesting for understanding the nucleon structure, and so on.

the 3He GPDs, in particular those accessible in the DVCS, could provide a new window for a better understanding of the structure of the neutron, and, in particular, of the orbital structure of its partonic constituents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neutron orbital angular momentum of 0.6 is obtained, which is in agreement with the most recent results of the JLab experiment E01-011.
the neutron GPD information, which can be accessed in the coherent DVCS on 3He, is not only interesting per se but it is also crucial for a better understanding of the proton GPDs.
3He and 4He are very interesting targets to study GPDs and DVCS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutron contribution to the 3He GPDs, which is the only one accessible in the coherent DVCS, is not negligible.
3He can be a good candidate for the extraction of neutron GPDs, and therefore of neutron orbital structure.
3He, in the framework of the IA, is the best nucleus for the extraction of neutron GPDs.
